;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]]
**The [[United Nations]] humanitarian coordinator for [[Libya]] condemns the cut-off of water supply to the capital [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]], after an armed group seized a [[Great Man-Made River]] control station. The armed group is reportedly using the water cut-off, affecting two million people, to secure the release of detained family members. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/04/condemns-water-cutoff-libyan-capital-tripoli-200411000610599.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[Chad]] reportedly ends its military participation with the [[Multinational Joint Task Force]] (MNJTF) countering [[Boko Haram]], saying [[Chadian ground forces]] will no longer operate outside its borders. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-chad-security-army/chad-army-will-stop-joining-regional-operations-against-jihadists-president-idUKKCN21T0JU?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Paul McCartney]]'s handwritten copy of [[The Beatles]]' "[[Hey Jude]]" is sold in a virtual [[auction]] for {{USD|910,000}}, almost six times its estimated value. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/04/11/us/the-beatles-paul-mccartney-hey-jude-trnd/index.html (CNN)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Anak Krakatoa]], part of the [[Krakatoa]] complex in [[Indonesia]]'s [[Sunda Strait]], erupts. [https://www.9news.com.au/world/krakatoa-volcano-eruption-world-indonesia-anak-krakatau/19f6d9d4-da0e-4825-8099-29823fc61b3a (Channel 9)]
*[[2020 Chernobyl Exclusion Zone wildfires]]
**A village near the mostly [[abandoned town]] of [[Poliske]] is evacuated, as [[forest fire]]s continue to spread inside the [[Chernobyl Exclusion Zone]], [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2020/04/10/village-evacuated-as-forest-fires-in-chernobyl-exclusion-zone-continue-to-burn (Euronews)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
****[[Brazil]] becomes the first country in the [[Southern Hemisphere]] to surpass 1,000 deaths from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], as the death toll rises to 1,068 and 19,789 total cases, according to [[Johns Hopkins University]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-52251342 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[Department of Health and Social Care]] reports 917 more deaths from COVID-19, bringing the [[United Kingdom|UK]]'s death toll to 9,875. Victims in the latest figures were aged between 11 and 102, while 33 people had no known underlying health conditions. [https://news.sky.com/story/coronavirus-scotland-records-47-new-coronavirus-deaths-taking-total-to-542-11971958 (Sky News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****With 20,071 deaths, the United States' death toll from COVID-19 passes [[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy|that of Italy]] and becomes the country with the highest number of known COVID-19 deaths in the world. [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/04/11/the-us-now-has-the-most-coronavirus-deaths-in-the-world-surpassing-italy.html (CNBC)]

;International relations
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Sudan]]'s Health Minister Akram Ali Altom says that his country urgently needs {{USD|120}}{{nbsp}}million to combat the COVID-19 pandemic. While the country has registered relatively few cases and two deaths, Altom says that if it spreads, the country is not prepared to face it. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-sudan/sudans-health-minister-says-country-needs-120-million-to-fight-coronavirus-idUSKCN21T0SY?il=0 (Reuters)]
